previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, and end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted after experiencing a seizure, severe headache, and visual disturbances. Initial evaluation revealed markedly elevated blood pressure, and MRI confirmed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), likely due to fluid overload. She underwent peritoneal dialysis, which normalized her blood pressure and resolved her neurological symptoms. Her home antihypertensive regimen was adjusted, discontinuing amlodipine and initiating verapamil and a low-dose metoprolol. Due to her history of PRES and use of bupropion, which can lower the seizure threshold, her bupropion dose was halved. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor blood pressure closely and follow up with her nephrologist and psychiatrist.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with no access and orthostasis leading to
syncope, with failed attempt at bedside central line placement.  The patient
has an elevated INR.

COMPARISON:  None.

PROCEDURE:
1.  Ultrasound-guided evaluation of the right internal jugular vein.
2.  Ultrasound-guided access of the right brachiocephalic vein.
3.  Placement of a 7 ___ triple-lumen non-tunneled catheter.
4.  Post-placement spot fluoroscopic image.

PHYSICIANS:  Drs. ___ and ___.  Dr. ___, the
attending radiologist, was present and supervising throughout the procedure.

MEDICATIONS:  1% local lidocaine.

PROCEDURE:  Prior to initiation of procedure, a written informed consent was
obtained and a preprocedure timeout was performed.  The right neck was prepped
and draped in sterile manner.  Initial attempt at ultrasound-guided access of
the right internal jugular vein was successful, though the wire could not be
advanced beyond the right IJV-brachiocephalic junction. Ultrasound evaluation
demonstrated high grade/complete occlusion of the right internal jugular vein
at its junction with the right brachiocephalic vein. Ultrasound evaluation of
the right neck demonstrated a prominent venous collateral extending from the
upper right internal jugular vein to the right brachiocephalic vein.  Under
ultrasound guidance hard copy images on file, the right brachiocephalic vein
was accessed with a micropuncture set, and the wire was advanced into the IVC.
A micropuncture sheath was placed, and the wire was exchanged for a 0.035
___ wire. Fascial dilatation was performed with a 6 ___ dilator, and a 7
___ triple-lumen non-tunneled catheter was placed such that the tip was in
the SVC.  The catheter was secured to the neck, and flushed and aspirated
well.  A final spot fluoroscopic image was obtained. Additionally, hard copy
images of ultrasound access were also obtained.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and was returned to the floor.

IMPRESSION:
1.  High grade/near-complete occlusion of the right internal jugular vein at
its junction with the right brachiocephalic vein.
2.  Successful placement of a 7 ___ non-tunneled central venous catheter
via the right brachiocephalic vein, with the tip in the SVC.  The line is
ready to use.

EXAM:  CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast obtained ___.

___.

HISTORY:  ___ female with elevated lactate and acidemia on peritoneal
dialysis, rule out infection.

TECHNIQUE:  After IV administration of contrast transaxial images from the
lung bases through the pelvis were obtained with routine protocol.

FINDINGS:

There is mild atelectasis at the right lung base.

The liver demonstrates homogeneous post-contrast enhancement without abnormal
enhancing mass identified.  The spleen, gallbladder, and adrenal glands are
unremarkable in appearance.  The native kidneys are shrunken.  Simple cyst is
identified within the left native kidney.  Transplant kidney in the right
lower quadrant is identified, somewhat atrophic when compared to the prior
study.  However, there still appears to have cortical function, as the cortex
is enhancing.

Visualized bowel is grossly unremarkable in appearance without bowel wall
thickening, inflammatory changes, or obstruction.  There is a significant
amount of fecal material noted throughout the colon.

A few foci of free air in the abdomen are likely related to peritoneal
dialysis.  Peritoneal dialysis catheter is noted within the pelvis.  There are
pockets of free fluid within the abdomen, likely related to patient's
peritoneal dialysis.  There is fluid in the lesser sac, along the anterior
aspect of the pancreas.  The adjacent pancreatic parenchyma looks unremarkable
in appearance, and this fluid is presumably from patient's peritoneal
dialysis, although in a somewhat unusual location.

No enlarged intraperitoneal, retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph nodes are
identified.

Abdominal aorta has a normal course and caliber.  

CT PELVIS:  Bowel loops are unremarkable in appearance.  Free fluid is likely
related to peritoneal dialysis.  Bladder is collapsed.  No enlarged lymph
nodes are identified.

Small compression fractures at the superior endplates of the T10 and T12
vertebral bodies are noted, likely chronic in nature.  Otherwise the osseous
structures are unremarkable in appearance.

There is no definable encapsulated fluid collection/abscess in the abdomen or
pelvis identified.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Pockets of free fluid within the abdomen and pelvis likely related to
patient's peritoneal dialysis.  There is a small amount of fluid along the
anterior aspect of the pancreas within the lesser sac which is in somewhat
atypical location for peritoneal dialysis fluid.  However the adjacent
pancreas is unremarkable in appearance, however correlation with lipase and
amylase may be warranted.

2.  Otherwise grossly unremarkable CT of the abdomen without source of
infection.

3.  Right lower quadrant transplant kidney is somewhat more atrophic when
compared to the prior study.

INDICATION:  Large hematocrit drop with recent instrumentation of the right
internal jugular with elevated INR.  Evaluate for intrathoracic bleeding.

COMPARISON:  ___.

UPRIGHT AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  Right-sided central venous catheter tip
terminates within the mid SVC.  There are low inspiratory lung volumes. 
Linear opacities within the left lung base are similar to prior, and likely
represent atelectasis.  The right lung is grossly clear.  There are no pleural
effusions or pneumothoraces.  No acute osseous abnormalities are seen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute interval change from prior with stable left basilar
subsegmental atelectasis.

EXAM:  MRI brain.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Patient with positional nausea and recent history of
PRES, rule out general cause of nausea.

TECHNIQUE:  T1 sagittal and FLAIR T2 susceptibility and diffusion axial images
of the brain were acquired.  Comparison was made with the MRI, ___.

FINDINGS:  Since the previous study, the previously noted patchy T2
hyperintensities indicative of posterior reversible encephalopathy have
resolved.  No acute infarct seen.  No new signal abnormalities are identified.
No mass effect, midline shift or hydrocephalus seen.  A small focus of
hyperintensity of nonspecific nature in the left frontal subcortical region is
unchanged.  Minimal periventricular hyperintensities are also unchanged. 
There is no evidence of intra- or extra-axial hemorrhage or fluid collection.

On the sagittal T1-weighted images, subtle increased signal is seen in the
basal ganglia bilaterally, this is a nonspecific finding and indicate
demineralization and could be related to hepatic or renal insufficiency. 
Clinical correlation recommended.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial abnormalities.  No infarcts.  Previously
noted abnormalities on the MRI of ___ have resolved.  No significant new
findings.
